claim_verdicts.evidence: options.md: "The Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) or Encapsulation: Scenarios (classes) that depend on configuration settings depend only on the configuration settings that they use." Same principle (depend only on what you use); the lesson's split-into-small-interfaces half follows directly and is outline item 1.

interfaces.md: "A class or struct that implements an interface must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)." interface.md: "Member bodies in an interface are the *default implementation*." None of IFullNotifier's three members has a body (NotifierIspViolation.cs:7-12 @ stage-1). Round 2 wording "every method IFullNotifier declares — all three" holds for this interface.

Ran: stage-1 NotifierIspViolation.cs with Retry changed to Retry(int orderId, int attempt), dotnet build (SDK 10, net10.0) -> "error CS0535: 'SmsOnlyNotifier' does not implement interface member 'IFullNotifier.Retry(int, int)'". Docs: "must provide an Equals method that matches the interface signature".

git show stage-1:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/NotifierIspViolation.cs lines 7-26: three members as stated; Send => Console.WriteLine($"sms about order {orderId}: {subject}"); History => throw new NotSupportedException("this channel keeps no history"); Retry => throw new NotSupportedException("this channel does not retry").

INotifier.cs:5-8 declares only void Send(int orderId, string subject). NotifierBase.cs:5 "public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier", :18 "protected abstract string Format(int orderId, string subject);", EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier (:21, :27) override only Format.

Ran: static void Use(IFullNotifier n); Use(new SmsNotifier()); against stage-1 sources, dotnet build -> "error CS1503: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'DonHang.Samples.Oop.SmsNotifier' to 'DonHang.Samples.Design.IFullNotifier'". UseSmall(INotifier) with SmsNotifier/EmailNotifier produced no error.
claim_verdicts.source: local build in scratchpad against examples/don-hang @ stage-1

claim_verdicts.evidence: Follows from code: IFullNotifier exposes History() publicly to any holder (interface members without body are implicitly public, interface.md:30) and SmsOnlyNotifier.History throws NotSupportedException (NotifierIspViolation.cs:21-22); nothing in the type tells the caller which implementation it holds.

Design reasoning derived from the ISP definition in claim 1 (per-dependent need, not method count); worded conditionally in the lesson ("fine when every caller and every implementer needs all three"). No factual/version content.

git show stage-1:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/NotifierIspViolation.cs line 14: "// SmsNotifier only ever sends. It still has to answer for History and Retry —"; line 16: "public sealed class SmsOnlyNotifier : IFullNotifier". The comment sits directly above SmsOnlyNotifier and names SmsNotifier.

issues.text: "crashes" states more than the code shows. SmsOnlyNotifier.History throws NotSupportedException (claim 4); whether the hypothetical support screen crashes depends on whether it handles the exception, which the lesson does not show. The q4 context can keep "crashes" because it describes one screen's outcome as a given scenario.
issues.quote: and a support screen that asks any `IFullNotifier` for its `History()` crashes the first time it is handed this one
issues.fix: Replace "crashes the first time it is handed this one" with "gets a `NotSupportedException` the first time it is handed this one".

issues.text: The misconception as worded says every implementing class uses every method. If that were true, no implementer would carry filler and the correction would not apply. The correction then argues against a different belief (each method used by some class somewhere) and cites SmsOnlyNotifier, which does not use History, contradicting the premise. I had to re-read twice to see which belief is being corrected.
issues.quote: "A big interface is fine as long as every class implementing it eventually uses every method somewhere."
issues.fix: Reword the belief to match the correction and q2: "A big interface is fine as long as each of its methods is used by some class somewhere in the system." Update the same text in q2 option a's `misconception` field.

issues.text: Summary line 5 gives a reason for fat interfaces (a wish for every channel to look the same) that no section mentions. The lesson never says why someone built IFullNotifier in the first place.
issues.quote: Cut interfaces by what each caller and implementer needs, not by a wish for every channel to look the same.
issues.fix: End line 5 after "needs" (e.g. "Cut interfaces by what each caller and implementer needs, not by how many methods they have."), which section 6 established; or add one sentence in section 4 saying IFullNotifier bundles the three so every channel looks the same.

issues.text: The clause implies an interface can give a method a body. Known vocab and prereqs present an interface only as a list of methods with no bodies, so I stopped here. The next words ("none of these three has one") let me go on, so the main idea is not blocked. q1's correct explanation repeats the same idea.
issues.quote: apart from any the interface already gives a body to — and none of these three has one
issues.fix: Drop the clause: "C# requires a class to provide every method the interface declares." Make the same cut in q1's correct explanation (en and vi).

issues.text: Section 4 prose names the IFullNotifier arrow and says "the three arrows around INotifier and NotifierBase" but never names EmailNotifier or SmsNotifier or says what "derives from" shows here; they appear only in section 5. I could narrate it only because foundation introduced these classes.
issues.quote: the three arrows around `INotifier` and `NotifierBase` are the small one
issues.fix: Replace with: "the other three arrows are the small one: `NotifierBase` implements `INotifier`, and `EmailNotifier` and `SmsNotifier` derive from it."

issues.text: The situation describes the code, not a moment: nobody in Đơn Hàng does anything or gets surprised. The question at the end is answered, so it still connects. The q4 context (a support screen crashing on History) is the kind of moment I could picture.
issues.quote: The class compiles, the interface looks complete, and yet two of its three methods cannot do what they promise. What went wrong?
issues.fix: Add one sentence before the question in which a developer passes a SmsOnlyNotifier to code that calls History() and it throws NotSupportedException.

issues.text: q1: options b and c are false on their face to anyone who has seen INotifier/IFullNotifier or any class implementing an interface, and d is off-topic. I can pick a without reading section 4.
issues.quote: An interface in C# may declare at most one method
issues.fix: Replace b or c with a plausible distractor from the lesson, e.g. "Its `Send` method has the wrong parameters for `IFullNotifier`".

issues.text: q4 option b explanation introduces an idea the lesson never discussed (when catching every exception would be right), which made me doubt option b rather than settle it.
issues.quote: Catching everything would matter when failures were rare and expected
issues.fix: Shorten to: "Catching the exception only hides that the interface promised something `SmsOnlyNotifier` cannot do." (en and vi).
